 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This
Day, Order Was Made Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice V Srishananda
 Oral Order
1. Heard Sri Sameer, learned counsel for the revision petitioner and learned High Court Government
Pleader for respondent-State.

2. Accused person who suffered an order of conviction in C.C.No.220/2010 dated 06.08.2013 on the file of Civil Judge and JMFC, Hosanagara for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and ordered to undergo Simple Imprisonment for a period of one year for the offence under Section 304(A) of IPC, which was confirmed in Crl.A.No.191/2013 dated 23.11.2015 on the file of the V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Shivamogga (Sitting at Sagar).

3. Facts in the nutshell for the disposal of the revision petition are as under:
3.1.

A complaint came to be lodged with Nagara Police Station alleging that on 27-9-2009, at about 3.00 NC: 2024:KHC:51183 p.m., when the complainant was heading towards the church from house on Nagara Masthikatte road, the accused,
being the driver of Bajaj Tempo Cruser Thoofan bearing Registration No.KA-15/4903 came from Nagara side in a rash and negligent manner and caused an accident by dashing to a boy, aged about 7 years, who was standing on the mud road in front of the bus stop, waiting to board a bus.
Because of the impact of the accident, the boy sustained grievous injuries as the vehicle ran over him.
Immediately, the injured was shifted to Nagara Hospital.
At about 4:55 p.m. and ultimately the boy succumbed to the injuries.
3.2. The rashness of the accused was complained of by contending that after hitting the boy, the body was dragged for about 20 feet and stopped the Bus.
3.3. Based on the complaint, Nagara Police Station registered a case in Crime No.44/2009 for the offenses punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
After registering the case, the Nagara Police Station conducted a detailed investigation and filed a charge sheet against the accused.
5. The presence of the accused was secured and a plea was recorded.
The accused pleaded not guilty

;
therefore, a trial was held.

sentences.text:
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, in all six witnesses were examined as PW-1 to PW-6 and 11 documentary evidence were placed on record, which was exhibited and marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P11, comprising of spot mahazar, inquest mahazar, motor vehicles inspection report,
postmortem report, rough sketch of place of incident, photographs, complaint and FIR.

7. The detailed cross-examination of prosecution witnesses did not yield any positive material,
except PW-1 made a stray admission in his cross-examination that the complaint is not signed by him.

For the reasons best known to the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor, did not NC:
2024:KHC:51183 choose to treat PW-1 as hostile witness to the extent he did not admit the complaint lodged by him.

8. The accused's statement as is contemplated under Section 313 of CRPC was recorded, wherein the accused denied all the incriminating materials, had failed to offer any explanation as is contemplated under Section 313(4) of Cr.P.C. nor placed any defense of this case on record.

9. Thereafter, the learned trial magistrate heard the parties and convicted the accused and sentenced as referred to supra.
10.
Being aggrieved by the same, the accused filed an appeal before the District Court, Shivamogga in Crl.A.No.191/2013.

The learned Judge in the First Appellate Court, after securing the records,
heard the parties in detail and dismissed the appeal of the accused, inter alia, in paragraphs 16 to 26 has held as under:

"16. PW.1 complainant has stated that on that day when he was going towards bus stand from his house by walk at that time he NC: 2024:KHC:51183 saw one Trax vehicle came in a high speed on wrong side and dashed against one child who was standing on the mud road and caused this accident.
As a result said child sustained grievous injuries and he provided water to the child and CW.3 to 5 came to the spot and injured was shifted to the hospital.
Subsequently said child died in the hospital.
In this regard he has lodged the complaint.

17. In the course of his cross examination he has stick up to his version that on that day accused drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and caused this accident, as a result said child sustained grievous injuries and died during the treatment in the hospital.
18. PW.2 Rohan Desa is the brother of the deceased.

He has stated that on that day himself and his brother were waiting for the bus at Kabale bus stop and at that time one vehicle driven by the accused from Nagar side came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his brother and caused this accident.
As a result, his brother has sustained grievous injuries and died in the hospital.
NC: 2024:KHC:51183 Sreedhara vs State By Psi on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19204398/
3 19. PW.3 Anthony Seckwera has stated that after hearing the noise from the Kabale bus stop he went to the spot and saw that there was a accident in which one boy has sustained injuries.
20. PW.4 John Bruganja is a spot pancha has stated that police have drawn spot mahazar in his presence as per Ex.P.1.
21. PW.5 Purushottama and PW.6 Ananda are the police witnesses who have deposed regarding their part in the investigation.
22. Of the prosecution witnesses PW.1 and 2 are the eye witnesses.

PW.1 is the bystander while PW.2 is none other than the elder brother of the deceased and both of them were waiting for the bus at the bus stop.
23.
On perusal of the sketch and spot panchanama, it discloses that the accident in- fact had taken place when the vehicle being driven by the accused came on a kachha road to the extent of 4 feet.
The tar road at the accident spot was measuring 13 feet in the width.
The vehicle being Bajaj Tempo Cruser Thoofan there was no difficulty for the driver to drive the vehicle on Tar road itself.
There appears to be no necessity for him to drive NC: 2024:KHC:51183 the vehicle on kachha road as has happened.
Even otherwise he should have been diligent in driving the vehicle by leaving the tar road.
Considering the fact that several persons were standing on kachha road for vehicle to go to some other place, undisputedly, PW.2 and deceased were among them.

24. Even on perusal of the evidence of PW.1 and 2 defence side has not been able to elicit anything in the cross examination that could destroy the version in the chief examination or to render their version unbelievable.

The defence side has not come up with any plausible explanation as to what compelled the accused to drive the vehicle on kachha road by leaving the tar road so wide enough to pass the vehicle in question.

25. The factum of death of boy 7 years old child in a road accident is undisputed and that is why concerned documents like inquest mahazar, P.M.Report, MVI Report etc.,
are marked with the consent of defence side.

26. As far as other prosecution witnesses are concerned, they are circumstantial witnesses and there is nothing worth to discuss as their evidence is not helpful so as to ascertain the rashness and negligence on the part of the NC: 2024:KHC:51183 accused driver.

The learned Magistrate in my considered opinion has properly appreciated the materials available on record and no fault can be found with the said finding. In- fact compensation awarded is very less compared to what could have been awarded.

As far as sentence of imprisonment is concerned, it is quite adequate considering the facts and circumstances of the case like death of a 7 years child that was standing by the side of the road waiting for the bus."

sentences.text: Being further aggrieved by the same, the accused is before this Court in this revision petition.

12. Sri Sameer, learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner, reiterating the grounds urged in the revision petition vehemently contended that when the complainant himself has not supported the case of the prosecution by virtue of a categorical admission in his cross-examination that complaint is not filed by him and thumb impression of the complainant was not marked by the prosecution, there was no basis at all for the learned trial judge to proceed with the case and then convict the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:51183 accused, which has not been properly appreciated by the learned judge in the First Appellate Court, which resulted in miscarriage of justice and sought for allowing the revision petition.

13. Alternatively, Sri Sameer, learned counsel contended that the accused is a poor and his brother-in-law's marriage is scheduled to be held on 26.12.2024, this Court may enhance the fine amount by setting aside the imprisonment.

He also pointed out that he has got a family to maintain and young children to be maintained and taking note of the same, the imprisonment of one year for the offence under Section 304(A) IPC needs to be set aside by enhancing the fine reasonably, which can be paid as compensation to the family of the deceased.
14. Per contra, Smt.Waheeda.M.M., learned High Court Government Pleader supports the impugned order.

She further contended that only on the ground that the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor did not mark the left thumb - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:51183 impression on the complaint, the entire case of the prosecution cannot be doubted.

15. She further contended that criminal law can be set into motion by anybody and at the most, if the complainant has not admitted his left thumb impression on the complaint, the death of 7 year old boy and the accident cannot be doubted having regard to the other material evidence on record.
Hence, she sought dismissal of the case.

16. In so for as the alternative submission is concerned, Smt. Waheeda contended that when the accused has gone to the extent of denying the very accident itself, showing any leniency to such a person is impermissible in the law and sought for dismissal of the revision petition in toto.
17. Having heard the parties in detail, this Court perused the material available on record meticulously.
18. On such perusal of the materials on record, the following points would arise for consideration.

5 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:51183 1.
Whether the revision petitioner is successful in establishing that the impugned judgments are suffering from legal infirmity or perversity and thus call for interference?
2. whether the sentence is excessive?
3. what order?

RE.POINT No.1:
19.

In the case on hand, the death of a 7 year old boy in a road traffic accident that occurred on 27.09.2009 at about 3.00 P.M. near the bus stand is established by placing necessary oral and documentary evidence on record.

Admittedly, accused was the driver of Bajaj Tempo Cruser Thoofan bearing Registration No.KA-15/4903.
20.
A rashness of the driving of the accused is found from the place of accident and the place, where the injured was lying which is about 20 feet away.

The only lacuna in the case of prosecution that the revision petitioner is banking upon in trying to assail with the impugned orders, is the admission made by PW-1 in his - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:51183 cross-examination.
In his cross-examination, PW-1 has admitted that he has not signed the complaint.
Admittedly, PW-1 is a person, who has subscribed his left thumb impression on the complaint.

For reasons best known to the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor, he neither marked the left thumb impression of the complainant on the complaint by confronting the same nor treated him as a hostile witness to the extent of PW-1 not admitting the lodging of complaint.

21. The trial magistrate could have also been little more careful by exercising the power vested in him under section 165 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 if the Assistant Public Prosecutor has failed to discharge his duty properly.

22. Merely on the ground that the complainant did not identify his thumb impression on the complaint and answering that he has not file the complaint itself would not be sufficient enough to doubt the case of the prosecution.

Moreso, having regard to the other witnesses - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:51183 supporting the case of the prosecution coupled with the other documentary evidence on record namely, Spot Mahazar, IMV report, Postmortem Report and Inquest Report.

sentences.text: Admittedly, there is no explanation forthcoming from the accused with regard to the accident.
Indemnity bond executed by the owner of the vehicle would go to show that vehicle was seized by the Police pursuant to the complaint lodged by the PW-1 in Crime No.40/2009.
He got released the vehicle from the custody of the Police and at that juncture, the owner of the vehicle has specifically admitted about the accident.

24. All these factors were stood cumulatively, prosecution is successful enough in establishing that regal a 7 years old boy lost his life on account of the accidental injuries sustained on 27.09.2009,
wherein the vehicle involved is Bajaj Tempo Cruser Thoofan bearing Registration No.KA-15-4903 and there is no dispute as to - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:51183 the accused is a driver of the said vehicle as on the date of the accident.
25.

In a matter of these nature, after the prosecution establishes his case by placing cogent evidence on record, the same has to be put to the accused seeking his explanation about the incriminatory materials found in the case of the prosecution while recording the accused statement as is contemplated under section 313 of Cr.P.C.
26.
The purpose of recording the accused statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. is not an empty formality or purposeless.
Firstly, the said procedure would allow sufficient opportunity for the accused to place his explanation to the incriminatory circumstances.
27. Secondly, the accused is given a chance to place his version about the incidence.

If in a given case, if the accused fails to deliberately utilized such opportunity, consequences in law will have to follow as is held in the case of RAVI KAPUR VS. STATE OF RAJASTHAN reported in (2012)9 SCC 284.
- 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:51183 28.

entities.text: RAVI KAPUR VS. STATE OF RAJASTHAN reported in (2012)9 SCC 284
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of material evidence on record held cumulatively, a stray admission in the cross- examination of PW-1 is not sufficient to hold that the entire case of the prosecution is to be doubted.

29. Accordingly, recording an order of conviction by the Trial magistrate confirmed by the First Appellate Court as referred supra does not call for interference that too in the revisional jurisdiction by this Court.
Hence, point No.1 is answered in the negative.

RE.POINT No.2:
Sreedhara vs State By Psi on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19204398/
7 30.
In the case on hand, a seven year old boy is done to death by the rash negligent driving of the accused.
The accused did not stop the vehicle on the spot but dragged the injured for a distance about 20 feet as could be seen from the material on record.
The same itself is enough to assess the rashness and negligence on the part of accused by applying the principles of res ipsa Loquitur.

Taking note of these aspects of the matter, learned magistrate has imposed imprisonment for a period of one year for the offence punishable under section 304(A) of IPC.
32.

In the attendant facts and circumstances, taking note of the age of the accused, family to be maintained etc., this Court is of the considered opinion that granting of one year imprisonment needs a reduction for a period of six months following the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Punjab V/s. Saurabh Bakshi reported in (2015) 5 SCC 182.

entities.text: State of Punjab V/s. Saurabh Bakshi reported in (2015) 5 SCC 182
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly Point No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

RE.POINT No.3:
33.

In view of the findings of this Court in Point Nos.1 and 2 as above, the following:
ORDER i) Criminal Revision Petition is allowed in part.

ii) While maintaining the order of conviction for the offences punishable under section 279 - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:51183 and 304(A) IPC, the imprisonment period of one year ordered by the trial Magistrate confirmed by the First appellate Court for the offence punishable under section 304(A)
of IPC, is reduced to six months.
iii) The rest of the sentences stands unaltered.
iv) The revision petitioner/accused is given time till 10.01.2025 to surrender before the learned Trial Magistrate.

Sd/-
(V SRISHANANDA)
